account: The International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) publishes a case document of its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) for source KAZ_S_136. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models to notify governments and companies. The source is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°, and the case document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by the EnMAP instrument of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. The document records that emissions were last detected on 12 March 2026, and UNEP updated it on 15 April 2026. On 5 May 2026 The Chemical Engineer relayed UNEP's snapshot and counted one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. A footnote to the case document states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed mitigation of a Kazakhstan gas pipeline that released an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither the trade report nor the September snapshot gives a case identifier, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established. UNEP's October 2026 snapshot reports a separate Kazakhstan pipeline leak of an estimated 200 tonnes over one week that was mitigated after a MARS notification, and its text gives no case identifier. On 22 October 2026 UNEP's MARS case studies page named the site as Kamenistoe and still listed KAZ_S_136 as a mitigation case for March 2026.

ai_role.statement: UNEP's case document records detection, notification, the operator's rerouting of gas and satellite confirmation. It names DLR's EnMAP for the plume image. The only description of an AI role is UNEP's general statement that IMEO analyzes satellite data with advanced AI models. The AI contribution to this specific detection is therefore not isolated. The sources are UNEP's own (system operator) plus trade press relaying UNEP. No operator or government statement is among the sources.

fields.account: The International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) publishes a case document of its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) for source KAZ_S_136. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models to notify governments and companies. The source is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°, and the case document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by the EnMAP instrument of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. The document records that emissions were last detected on 12 March 2026, and UNEP updated it on 15 April 2026. On 5 May 2026 The Chemical Engineer relayed UNEP's snapshot and counted one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. A footnote to the case document states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed mitigation of a Kazakhstan gas pipeline that released an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither the trade report nor the September snapshot gives a case identifier, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established. UNEP's October 2026 snapshot reports a separate Kazakhstan pipeline leak of an estimated 200 tonnes over one week that was mitigated after a MARS notification, and its text gives no case identifier. On 22 October 2026 UNEP's MARS case studies page named the site as Kamenistoe and still listed KAZ_S_136 as a mitigation case for March 2026.

purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators and governments mitigate them. This case was that purpose.

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary is identified. The benefit is an avoided greenhouse-gas release.
The operator rerouted gas to stop the leak, and no gain to the operator itself, such as recovered gas or an avoided cost, is reported.

The site is one source among thousands of MARS alerts, and the trade press counts over 3,500 alerts and about 43 confirmed cases since 2023. The subsequent emissions observed in May 2026 limit the climate benefit.
